doc.title: Jon Jang interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 17, 2003 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Measuring his own level and Robeson's closing quote
summary: Creating by his own standards while measuring against the greats, and Robeson's line on culture over might.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Well I’m trying to but then you can’t just listen to yourself either. Because then you’re not really raising the level. That’s why you have to always measure your music by what these great artists did and then try to — not be like them — well not be like them — be like them in the way of just being, just creating and committing to do that, and not being distracted by all these other things, with things that go on in the world. Maybe that’s the inference of your question about what do you think about the world now, is that yeah for artists, okay maybe I can end with like a quote that Paul Robeson said. A great culture — or he said — a great civilization is measured by its culture, not by its might. And so that’s why for us as artists we have to continue to create an alternative to war and violence and what we’re doing is creating values that we want to bring people back to. We don’t want © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
to invent new ways to kill people. And not only costly ways, and I don’t mean economically, but cost in terms of lives.
But what does that have to do with the jazz archive? I don’t know. MR I think it’s a worthy contribution.
